name: Percentime
subtitle: Spans filling as they pass

sections.title: The calendar opens six spans for you
body: Open the app and today, this week, this month, this quarter and this year are already there. You enter no start and no goal. The moment a span ends, the next one opens.

sections.title: The span is cut into cells
body: A percentage alone is hard to place. So the span is cut to the unit one step down. A day is 24 hours, this week is 7 days, this quarter is 14 weeks, this year is 12 months. Spans that do not land on calendar units get their units grouped instead.

sections.title: Read it from the Lock Screen
body: Three Lock Screen widgets, three Home Screen widgets, and a stack widget that holds several spans at once. Every size carries the timer name, so you know which span the percentage belongs to. The same widgets come up large in StandBy. Turn the phone sideways and the app itself switches to a black screen with the ring and a large percentage. They redraw at the very moment the number changes, so at noon the day reads exactly 50 percent.

sections.title: Pick how you read it
body: The same span can be read several ways. Tap the number on the full screen and the readings you picked come round in turn. You set the decimal places on the progress reading with one tap on a row of cells from 0 to 6: one place as it comes, the second onward with Pro.

items: Years, months, days and a clock

sections.title: Say it, and the start and goal fill in
body: Tap the three-strand icon at the top right of New Timer and the app starts listening at once. Say "until 2", "3 hours" or "meeting 1 hour 30 minutes", stop, and the start, goal and title fill in. You tap Save yourself. The icon is there in every app language except the 11 that have no Apple speech recognizer.

By hand, you choose between "From now" and "Start and goal". With "From now" you turn only an hours and minutes wheel, and the count starts the moment you save. Leave the title blank and it takes a number, as in "Timer 1" and "Timer 2".

faq.q: What do I see when I first open it
a: Today, this week, this month, this quarter and this year are already there. Nothing to enter. The 2020s have no card of their own and sit as one row in the stack at the top of the first screen. You can take that row out in Choose rows or pick the 2020s in a widget.
The card at the top is the stack. Short spans sit above, long ones below. Choose rows sets what goes there.

faq.q: What happens when a span ends
a: A calendar span hands over to the next one the moment it ends. A repeating timer stays at 100 percent after a round until the start of the day its next round begins, then drops to 0 percent and fills again from the start time. If the next round starts later the same day, it drops to 0 percent as soon as the round ends. It also shows how long until the next round.
A timer of your own that passes its goal does not stop there: the time past the goal stacks up in the accent color.

The span is cut to the unit one step down. A day is 24 hours, this week is 7 days, this month is about 30 days, this quarter is 14 weeks, this year is 12 months, the 2020s are 10 years. Spans that do not land on calendar units get their units grouped: 35 days become 5 weeks, 90 minutes become 30 cells of 3 minutes.

faq.q: How are the decimal places chosen
a: The span decides. A day is whole numbers, a week one place, a month and a quarter two, a year three, several years four. They are picked so the last digit moves about every ten or twenty minutes.

Pick the progress reading and set the places yourself and that value is used. You set them in Settings and in Edit Timer with one tap on a row of cells from 0 to 6. More places also means a finer redraw: six places redraw up to thirty times a second. Without Pro the reading is cut at one place.

In Settings each place gets its own value: In the app, Lock Screen, StandBy and Home Screen. "In the app" sets the default number of places; each of the others sets the most that place will show. Without Pro, every place marks the cells from 2 to 6 as Pro, and tapping one of them opens the purchase screen. A place's "Same as the app" chip also shows the app's setting, as in "Same as the app (2)".

faq.q: The ring in the middle of the full screen
a: The span is cut into cells and laid around a ring. The percentage sits large in the centre with the count of filled cells beneath it. A span that does not divide into cells is drawn as one unbroken ring.

There are three colours. Cells behind you set in ink, the one cell filling now in the accent, and the cells ahead left as a pale line. When the span fills, the accent leaves the screen. That is how arrival is shown.

faq.q: How often do the widgets change
a: They are redrawn the moment the percentage changes. A day widget gains one percent every 14 minutes 24 seconds and reads exactly 50 percent at noon. A span of 30 days is redrawn every 4 minutes 19 seconds.
Tap the plus button and choose New timer or Add a calendar span. A new timer is set one of two ways, "From now" or "Start and goal", and it opens on the one you picked last time.
With "From now" you turn only an hours and minutes wheel, from 1 minute to 23 hours 59 minutes, and the count starts the moment you save. A span of a day or more is set with "Start and goal".

"Start and goal" opens with the start at now and the goal a week later. Chips inside the two fields change them at once: the start to the beginning of today or this month, the goal to a day, 30 days, 100 days or a year later, or to a moment such as the end of this week. Tap a field to open its calendar, and a separate time wheel appears below it.
The title can stay blank. The timer then takes the lowest free number, as in "Timer 1" and "Timer 2", and you can rename it later in Edit Timer.

Tap the three-strand icon at the top right of New Timer and the app starts listening at once. When you stop speaking, it fills the start, goal and title with what it understood, and you tap Save yourself. The icon is there only when making a new timer, and it hides when Weekly hours is on.

"until 2" runs to the next 2 o'clock, and "3 hours" or "1 hour 30 minutes" run that long from now. "from Nov 5 to Dec 31" runs from the start of November 5 to the end of December 31. It also understands "until tomorrow", "until Friday 6pm" and "100 days". Say "meeting 1 hour 30 minutes" and meeting becomes the title.

The icon appears in every app language except the 11 that have no Apple speech recognizer, such as Bengali and Tamil. On first use the app asks once for microphone and speech recognition access. On an iPhone that cannot run speech recognition on the device, a typing field opens, and you type the phrase there.

Four. A combination of units such as years, months, days and a clock; one unit as a decimal; progress in percent; and life units. Life units count full moons, weekends, springs and birthdays, and they are part of Pro.
Tap the number on the full screen and the readings come round in turn. Progress is left out of that turn because the big number already shows it.
A timer with Notify me when the goal arrives turned on sends one notification at the goal. The calendar spans do not use it, so nothing arrives every night.

Span alerts are part of Pro. They arrive when the span reaches 25, 50, 75 or 100 percent, whichever you picked. Points still ahead in this turn are scheduled, and opening the app sets up the next turn.

The six calendar spans, all six timer widget sizes, the stack widget and syncing between devices work without Pro. You keep three timers of your own, and the calendar spans never count toward that. One timer with Weekly hours works without Pro too. Progress shows one decimal place without Pro. Setting a new timer with the From now wheel works without Pro too. Setting one by voice also works without Pro (except in the 11 languages with no Apple speech recognizer).

Runs on iPhone with iOS 18 or later. The app and its widgets come in 46 languages and follow your device language. Use it upright, or turn it sideways for a large black screen. Light is the default and it flips to black when the system is dark.

privacy.title: Percentime Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: Percentime collects no personal data. There is no account and no sign-in, and Apple handles the Pro purchase.
intro: kvndh (the developer) handles the personal data of users of the Percentime app (the app) as described below.

sections.title: Purposes of processing
paragraphs: The app has no sign-up or login, and the developer does not process personal information about its users, so there is no purpose to state.

sections.title: Personal information processed
paragraphs: The developer collects no personal information. The app works with the data below, and the developer does not receive any of it. What the app hears when you set a timer by voice is not kept, and everything else is kept in the app's storage on your device.
bullets: Your timers (name, start and goal, repeat rule, alert points, reading settings): used to draw the values on screen and in widgets
Settings (which rows go in the stack): used to lay out the app
The month and day of your birthday: used only to count birthdays ahead when you pick that life unit
Whether Pro was bought: used to decide which features open in the app and widgets

What you say when setting a timer by voice: recognized on the device and used only to fill the start, goal and title of a new timer. The audio and the full transcript are not kept; when you tap Save, only the values in the start, goal and title fields go into your timers above (microphone and speech recognition access is optional and asked for once, on first use; if you decline, the typing field and every other feature still work, and you can turn access off in the Settings app)

sections.title: Retention period
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal data. Everything in the app's storage is removed when the app is deleted. Timers stay until you delete them, and the calendar spans roll into the next span rather than piling up.

sections.title: Provision to third parties
paragraphs: Personal information is not provided to third parties.

sections.title: Outsourcing of processing
paragraphs: No processing is outsourced. The Percentime Pro purchase is handled by Apple on the App Store, and payment information follows Apple's privacy policy. Your own iCloud is used to keep timers and settings in step between devices. The developer receives no payment method, no Apple Account information and nothing held in iCloud.

sections.title: Destruction of personal information
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal data, so there is nothing to destroy. Delete a timer by swiping it in the list or from the More menu on its full screen, and delete everything in the app by deleting the app.

sections.title: Rights of users and legal representatives
paragraphs: Because the developer holds no personal information about you, there is nothing to access, correct or delete. If you have questions, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: What the app uses sits in the app's storage and in its App Group container, and the widgets read the same file. Timers and settings are kept in step with your other devices on the same Apple Account through your own iCloud. The developer runs no server. Notifications are local: made on the device and delivered on the device. Speech recognition for setting a timer by voice runs on the iPhone, and what it hears is not kept.

sections.title: Cookies and other automatic collection
paragraphs: The app uses no cookies, no advertising identifier and no analytics tools.

sections.title: Privacy officer
paragraphs: If you have questions about personal information, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Remedies
paragraphs: If you need advice about a privacy concern or help settling a dispute, you can contact the Korean bodies listed below. If you live outside Korea, you can also contact the data protection authority in your country.
bullets: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: 1833-6972 in Korea (www.kopico.go.kr)
Personal Information Infringement Report Center: 118 in Korea (privacy.kisa.or.kr)
Supreme Prosecutors' Office: 1301 in Korea (www.spo.go.kr)
National Police Agency: 182 in Korea (ecrm.police.go.kr)
European Union and EEA: the data protection authority of your country (edpb.europa.eu)
United Kingdom: Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk)
United States: Federal Trade Commission (reportfraud.ftc.gov)
Other countries: the data protection or consumer protection authority where you live

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: If this policy changes, this page will show the new text and its new effective date.
